files.about: Functional building definitions.
Numeric building type ids (stored per tile in TileMap.bld) and their keys.
Civilizations: creation (from bands, splits, secessions or presets), cultures and languages, identity (name, color, emblem), personality, and extinction (kept in history).
How civilizations end.
ETHOS: what a society values, and therefore how it works.
Civ knowledge of the map (non-omniscient AI).
NATIONAL MISSIONS: the goal a nation is pursuing right now.
Settlements: founding, the monthly cycle (economy -> demography -> construction -> health/migration), yearly upkeep (territory, education, access), transfer between civilizations and destruction.
Territory: each settlement projects influence over nearby tiles (stronger with population, culture, administration and transport).

Urban development. Each settlement runs at most one construction project at a time, chosen by utility from its measured needs (housing pressure, food deficit, material shortages, unworked deposits, energy deficit, services per capita, threats, transport links)
Balance parameters. Every gameplay coefficient lives here (not scattered as magic numbers) so it can be tuned, tested for sensitivity and adjusted at runtime from the developer panel.
Binary min-heap keyed by float priority, storing integer payloads.
Small numeric helpers shared by all systems.
Seeded 2D simplex noise (after Stefan Gustavson's public-domain reference implementation of Ken Perlin's simplex noise), plus fractal helpers.
Deterministic, seedable pseudo-random number generation.
Simulation time scales.
Cultural change (yearly).
Procedural languages and name generation.

Procedural names for everything a civilization creates beyond its places and people: chronicles, printing houses, newspapers, broadcasters, social platforms, holographic networks, AI systems and the labs that build them.
Religion as a dynamic social institution.
SPORTS, LEAGUES AND WORLD GAMES (yearly).

Ecosystems: vegetation regrowth, animal herds (movement, grazing, logistic growth limited by local vegetation, predation, starvation, climate stress), human hunting, extinction, slow evolution into subspecies, and optional fantasy monsters.

Animal species. Habitat suitability, diet and growth parameters are stylized; predator–prey coupling follows Lotka–Volterra-style dynamics (prey growth limited by vegetation, predators by prey encounters).
National market & public finance (yearly).
Round 7: what people do for a living.

Settlement economy (monthly): labour allocation, food, materials, industry, energy, services and household consumption — all in physical units that flow through the settlement's food store and the civilization's national market stock.
Transport networks & trade (yearly).
Round 7: street traffic at real-world rates, derived (never saved, never changes history).

VISITOR ACCORDS (yearly): friendly nations at peace that both have a harbour (and later an airport) open their borders to each other's travellers: pilgrims and merchants by sea in the age of sail, tourists by air in the jet age.
Anthropogenic existential risks (speculative or plausible; magnitudes stylized).
Space programs & off-world settlement (yearly).

The PHOTO ALBUM: every 50 years each nation's capital and its largest other city are recorded as compact LAYOUT RECORDS (a few hundred bytes): for every column of the city from west to east, the tallest building and the nearest building with their types and ti

World history: every meaningful development is recorded as a HistoryEvent with the entities involved, a map location, an importance level and — for decisions such as wars, revolutions or collapses — the CAUSES that were actually measured when the decision was
The civilization feed: what people of the time read, heard or scrolled.

The interface AROUND the feed, in the medium of the nation's era: a cave wall, a scribe's tablet house, a scriptorium with a town crier, a printing house, a newspaper front page, a broadcast set, a social app or a holographic interface.
Era-appropriate headlines generated by deterministic templates from actual recorded events (no free-form narrative): ancient chronicles, broadsheets, modern news and futuristic feeds.
Time-series statistics sampled from live simulation state (yearly, with adaptive decimation so long histories stay bounded), plus change decomposition built from recorded demographic flows.
Media and artificial intelligence (yearly, per civilization).
How a civilization's news travels, from its adopted technology (no other dependencies).
Nuclear weapons: programmes, doctrine, deterrence, escalation, strikes, fallout, nuclear winter and arms control.
Warfare. ARMIES are raised from settlements' working-age people (reducing labour), equipped from the national ARMS stock and paid from the military budget.
Weapons by era, land doctrine, arms races and special operations.
Round 9: which device a save was made on.
Save-format migrations.
Local-first save storage in IndexedDB.
World serialization (save format v1).
Diplomacy (yearly). Relations between civs that have met are persistent state: opinion, trust, trade, shared border, disputed tiles, grievances (memory of wars and lost land), rivalry and treaties.
Government & internal politics (yearly).
Government forms are LABELS derived from a continuous institution vector (see Institutions in sim/types.ts) plus scale and era.
Leadership & succession.
Mobile groups: settlers (found new settlements), explorers (reveal the map), migrants & refugees (move people between settlements), missionaries (carry religion), colonists (overseas settlement).
Nomadic bands (individual-level hunter-gatherer groups).
Demography at two resolutions.
Character development over a lifetime (notable persons only).
Abstract public-health model.
Population accounting ledger.

Migration: people leave settlements suffering hunger, unrest or overcrowding and move toward known settlements that are more prosperous, better fed and have room — preferring their own civilization; foreign destinations depend on migration policies.
Individual persons: creation, inheritance (genes + traits), naming, death.
Personality traits of individuals.
Fictional horrors: GOD MODE ONLY.

God powers. Every power mutates simulation state (terrain, climate, people, institutions, technology, relations...) — never just a label — and is recorded in WorldState.interventions so a timeline can be reproduced.
Round 10: which god powers a world allows.
Undo for terrain-editing strokes: snapshots of each touched tile before the first change.

Terrain ground tiles (ter.*), mountains/hills (mtn.*), water details and shore pieces (shore.*)

Era transport (veh.*): riders, carriages, bicycles, trams, cars, buses, lorries, aircraft, personal flyers and ships, each with 2-4 animation frames (wheels, legs, rotors, paddles, wakes, thrusters).
Boats, ships, carts, trains, cars, aircraft, rockets (veh.*) Water and land vehicles: side view facing RIGHT (the renderer mirrors for leftward motion).
Sprite atlas: rasterizes every palette-keyed sprite into canvases once at startup, with lazily created team-colored variants (T/U/V keys replaced by a civilization's colors).
2D camera: world units are art pixels (1 tile = 8 px); zoom = CSS px per art px.
